Import a mass spectral library

Source: R/library.R
read_msp.Rd

Stream NIST-compatible MSP files into sparse in-memory or disk-backed storage. OpenChrom Agilent and Shimadzu exports and MoNA/Golm MSP fields are accepted.

Usage

read_msp(
  file,
  backend = c("auto", "memory", "sqlite"),
  db_file = NULL,
  batch_size = 1000L,
  source = basename(file),
  encoding = "UTF-8",
  origin = c("unknown", "experimental", "predicted"),
  strict = TRUE,
  max_spectra = Inf
)

open_library(path)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSlibrary'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

file

Local MSP file. Compressed files should first be extracted.

backend

Storage: auto uses SQLite for files larger than 100 MB.

db_file

SQLite output path; required for the sqlite backend. Auto storage uses a new file beside the MSP when this is omitted.

batch_size

Number of records buffered per transaction.

source

Library provenance, defaulting to the input filename.

encoding

Text encoding; UTF-8 input with Windows-1252 fallback is supported.

origin

Whether spectra are experimental, predicted or of unknown origin.

strict

Check the declared number of peaks against the parsed pairs.

max_spectra

Optional import limit, useful for previews.

path

Existing spectral-library SQLite file.

x

A GCMSlibrary object.

...

Additional printing arguments.

Value

A GCMSlibrary object. Memory objects contain sparse spectra; disk objects retain a path and open read-only connections when queried.

Details

MSP tags are case-insensitive. Repeated tags, synonyms and unknown fields remain available through library_metadata(raw=TRUE). Raw masses and intensities are retained as double precision arrays. Sparse matrix extraction sums duplicate masses; nominal binning and normalization are explicit options. Explicit Pseudocount/Ion_total tags retain a supplied full-spectrum total; library_search uses it for count-sensitive comparisons without changing raw peaks. In-memory libraries store a dgCMatrix plus compact metadata. Exceptional unsorted, duplicate or zero-intensity peak records retain exact raw arrays.

SQLite stores one pair of little-endian float64 blobs per spectrum, indexed metadata and a long retention-index table. Import is transactional and uses bounded batches. Library files can be moved and reopened with open_library(). Existing databases are never overwritten. No live connection is serialized.

Retention indices retain their raw field, phase class and provenance. NIST/OpenChrom comment summaries SemiStdNP, StdNP and StdPolar map to DB5, DB1 and DBWAX; slash-delimited uncertainty fields remain in the raw value. DB1, DB5 and DBWAX denote nonpolar, semi-standard nonpolar and polar classes; a separate column/stationary-phase field also supplies the RI phase class. An unspecified column remains unknown. Zero RI placeholders are omitted from the index table. Supplied SMILES are preserved without chemical canonicalization.

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext=".msp")
writeLines(c("Name: example", "Formula: C2H6O", "RI_DB5: 560",
             "Num Peaks: 3", "31 100; 45 60; 46 20;"), f)
lib <- read_msp(f)
lib
library_metadata(lib)
retention_indices(lib)
spectra(lib)
